test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two trains, Train A and Train B, are traveling towards each other on parallel tracks. Train A is 150 meters long and moves at a speed of 72 km/h. Train B is 100 meters long and moves at a speed of 54 km/h. How much time (rounded off to two decimal places) will it take for Train A to completely pass Train B?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Opposite direction ⇒ relative speed = sum

72 km/hr = 20 m/s, 54 km/hr = 15 m/s

Relative speed = 20 + 15 = 35 m/s

Total distance = 150 + 100 = 250 m

Time = 250 ÷ 35 ≈ 7.14 sec

**∴ Answer = 7.14 seconds**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of Train A = 150 m, Speed = 72 km/hr

Length of Train B = 100 m, Speed = 54 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Time = Total distance ÷ Relative speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Convert speeds into m/s

⇒ 72 km/hr = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s

⇒ 54 km/hr = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s

⇒ Relative speed (opposite direction) = 20 + 15 = 35 m/s

⇒ Total distance = 150 + 100 = 250 m

⇒ Time = 250 ÷ 35

⇒ Time ≈ 7.14 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 7.14 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When objects move in opposite directions, relative speed = sum of speeds.

Train Crossing Concept

Total distance covered = sum of lengths when crossing each other.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18.
